title: China's rare-earth technology-export suspension expires 2026-11-10: the reachable layer is magnet-manufacturing and separation capacity, not the miners
thesis: On 2025-10-09 China's Ministry of Commerce issued Announcements 61 and 62, expanding export controls across the rare-earth chain: Announcement 61 covers foreign-made products containing Chinese rare-earth content, and Announcement 62 specifically prohibits exporting TECHNOLOGY for rare-earth mining, smelting/separation, metal production, magnet manufacturing, and secondary-resource recycling. Both were suspended from 2025-11-07 to 2026-11-10 with no stated reason. That date is now roughly ten weeks away and nothing published as of this card commits to what happens next. General coverage runs this as a will-they-won't-they geopolitical story about Beijing's leverage, correctly noting that China still processes up to 90% of global rare earths and that, per CSIS, no country has yet replicated its integrated supply chain. What the coverage does not connect is the specific, investable layer the technology decree actually gates: who outside China can commission separation trains or magnet-sintering lines at all, decree or no decree. One confirmed listed name sits exactly on that layer: Neo Performance Materials (TSX: NEO), which operates the Silmet plant in Estonia, described as until recently the only industrial-scale rare-earth separation facility operating commercially in the Western hemisphere outside Asia, and is ramping its Narva magnet-manufacturing line from 2,000 to 5,000 tonnes/year. TASTE-001 is applied visibly here: this card is scoped to that separation/magnet-manufacturing layer and refuses the miner-equity framing (MP Materials, Lynas) the rule already flags as the crowded, already-retail trade.
why_now: The suspension's own clock, not a news cycle, sets the date: 2026-11-10 is fixed by MOFCOM's own announcement, not an estimate. The IEA's Global Critical Minerals Outlook states that full implementation of these controls would put USD 6.5 trillion a year of downstream production outside China at risk, with the automotive sector facing the single largest exposure at over USD 3 trillion, a figure serious enough that Reuters ran it as a warning the same day. Independent analysis as of mid-2026 frames three live outcomes for the deadline (extension, selective reinstatement, full reimposition) and none has been confirmed. Separately, President Trump has described the underlying US-China arrangement as renegotiated annually rather than a one-off, meaning this is a recurring catalyst inside the horizon, not a single pass-fail event. The reachable layer is also moving on its own timeline regardless of Beijing's decision: Neo Performance Materials' Narva ramp and Ucore Rare Metals' (TSXV: UCU) Louisiana separation complex are both under construction now.
retail_gap: The China-rare-earth-leverage story is covered exhaustively as diplomacy and as a rare-earth-miner rally (MP Materials +165%, Lynas +159% YoY), which is precisely the crowded trade TASTE-001 already refuses. What is not covered anywhere found this run is the technology-control angle tied to a specific investable capacity layer: which listed names actually hold separation or magnet-grade production capability outside China, and how the November 10 decision changes their competitive position. Neo Performance Materials' two-plant capacity ramp is discussed in specialist trade press (rare-earth-mining.com) and nowhere connected to the MOFCOM decision date in general financial coverage. The ownership and listing status of the rest of that layer (Vacuumschmelze, Solvay's rare-earth segment) remains genuinely unresolved by any source fetched this run or by Tally's prior appraisal (IMP-20260830-16), which is itself the honest measure of how thin the mapped reachable pool still is.

unmappedness.rationale: Held below 70 because this is close to a saturated macro theme: the suspension, the decree text, and China's processing dominance are all exhaustively covered, and the candidate's own campaign-record scoring (2026-08-30) already flagged this as 'close to a saturated theme.' Held at 58 rather than lower because the specific chain from the technology-transfer restriction to who can actually commission a separation train or a magnet-sintering line outside China is thinly mapped: Tally's impact appraisal (IMP-20260830-16, LEAKY band, public_reach scored 40) independently found that after correctly refusing the miner framing, only one confirmed listed name (Neo Performance Materials) carries real, described capacity, one more (Ucore) is pre-commercial, and the status of the sector's other most-cited capacity (Vacuumschmelze, Solvay) could not be established by any source fetched across two appraisal passes. That gap, not the decree itself, is what a chain build would need to close.

evidence.claim: Announcement No. 62 of 2025 of the Ministry of Commerce prohibits the export of technologies related to rare earth mining, smelting and separation, metal production, magnet manufacturing, and the recycling and utilization of secondary rare earth resources. Announcements No. 61 and 62 of 2025 are suspended from November 7, 2025 to November 10, 2026, and MOFCOM did not elaborate on the specific reasons for the suspension.
evidence.source_name: CIRS Group, China Temporarily Suspends Export Controls on Key Raw Materials
source_excerpt: Announcement No. 62 of 2025 of the Ministry of Commerce: Decision on Imposing Export Controls on Rare Earth-Related Technologies This announcement prohibits the export of technologies related to rare earth mining, smelting and separation, metal production, magnet manufacturing, and the recycling and utilization of secondary rare earth resources, including their carriers, as well as technologies for the assembly, debugging, maintenance, repair, and upgrading of related production lines.
This indicates that from November 7, 2025, to November 10, 2026, the export of these items and technologies will not be bound by the specific provisions of the previously mentioned announcements.
The Ministry of Commerce and the General Administration of Customs did not elaborate on the specific reasons for the suspension in the latest announcement.

evidence.claim: If China's rare earth export controls were implemented in full, the economic value of downstream production at risk would reach USD 6.5 trillion per year for countries outside China, with the automotive sector facing the single greatest impact at over USD 3 trillion in potential direct losses.
evidence.source_name: International Energy Agency, Global Critical Minerals Outlook (Rare Earth Elements analysis), as reported the same day by Reuters via Nikkei Asia
source_excerpt: If these rare earth export controls were implemented in full, the economic value of downstream production at risk would reach USD 6.5 trillion per year for countries outside China.

The automotive sector is set to face the single greatest impact with over USD 3 trillion in potential direct losses outside China, followed by electronics and other transport (aviation, trucks and trains) sectors.

evidence.claim: Neo Performance Materials' Silmet plant in Estonia (TSX: NEO) is described as, until recently, the only industrial-scale rare-earth separation facility operating commercially in the Western hemisphere outside Asia. Its Narva magnet plant targets 2,000 tonnes/year initially, scaling to 5,000 tonnes/year. Ucore Rare Metals (TSXV: UCU) is developing a Strategic Metals Complex in Louisiana using proprietary RapidSX separation technology and is not yet an operating refiner at commercial scale.
evidence.source_name: rare-earth-mining.com, Top 10 Rare Earth Refining Companies Outside China
source_excerpt: Neo Performance Materials (TSX: NEO) operates the NPM Silmet plant in Sillamäe, Estonia — until recently, the only industrial-scale REE separation facility operating commercially in the Western hemisphere outside of Asia.
The Narva magnet plant targets 2,000 tpa initially, scaling to 5,000 tpa
Ucore Rare Metals (TSXV: UCU) is developing a Strategic Metals Complex (SMC) in Louisiana, targeting rare earth separation using its proprietary RapidSX solvent extraction technology.
Ucore is not yet an operating refiner at commercial scale

evidence.claim: In the near term, supply chains remain heavily dependent on China, which continues to dominate processing, refining, and downstream manufacturing, and as a result China retains significant leverage over critical mineral supply chains.
evidence.source_name: CSIS, Rare Earth Export Restrictions One Year Later
source_excerpt: In the near term, supply chains remain heavily dependent on China, which continues to dominate processing, refining, and downstream manufacturing.
As a result, China retains significant leverage over critical mineral supply chains.

evidence.claim: China processes up to 90% of global rare earths, and no single country currently has the financial or technical capacity to replicate China's integrated supply chain, though MP Materials, USA Rare Earth, Lynas Rare Earths and Iluka Resources are named as the firms advancing alternative capacity.
evidence.source_name: Mining Technology, China rare earth export pause nears expiry amid persistent supply concentration
source_excerpt: China processes 'up to 90%' of global rare earths
no single country currently has the financial or technical capacity to replicate China's integrated supply chain
